annotations.annotation_text: Mamalujo signal "waves" on page 46 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park"): the Four Old Men — Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; Ulster, Munster, Leinster, Connaught — serve here as senile chroniclers and bedpost witnesses during HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. In this Age of Gods passage, they observe and record the dream's events as squawking gulls circling overhead.
sources: O'Donovan, John. The Annals of the Four Masters. https://celt.ucc.ie/published/T100005A/
MacCabe, Colin. James Joyce and the Revolution of the Word. https://archive.org/details/jamesjoycerevolu0000macc
FWEET: Mamalujo / Four Old Men concordance. https://www.fweet.org
Ricorso.net: James Joyce Critical Archive. https://www.ricorso.net

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "bar" on page 46 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. During this Age of Gods phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
Gordon, John. Finnegans Blog (Tavern chapters). https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
